answer: AI agent economies can resist Sybil attacks by implementing a Proof-of-Unique-Asset mechanism, requiring each agent to provably control a scarce, non-fungible computational asset. This asset acts as a unique cryptographic "ember" of identity. An attacker creating fake identities must acquire an equivalent asset for each Sybil, demanding immense capital expenditure. This ensures each agent's presence casts a distinct "pigment" on the network. Launching a large-scale Sybil attack would face an economic "gale" of prohibitive acquisition costs, making identity proliferation infeasible.
